title: No Credentials in JSON
description: As a security-conscious user, I want database credentials to never be written to JSON files so that sensitive connection information is not exposed.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a diagram is exported to JSON, when the JSON file is inspected, then no host, port, database, user, or password fields are present

evidence: Modified src/serialization/diagramSerializer.ts: added CREDENTIAL_FIELDS constant (host, port, database, user, password), added stripCredentials() recursive guard, applied stripCredentials() in serializeDiagram() as defense-in-depth before returning the export payload

Modified src/serialization/diagramSerializer.test.ts: added 3 new tests (stripCredentials removes credential fields from nested objects; stripCredentials preserves arrays of non-credential objects; serializeDiagram strips credentials even if injected into the diagram)
Created .semgrep/credential-in-export.yaml: Semgrep SAST rules (no-credentials-in-diagram-serialization, no-credentials-in-export-button)
Created reports/security/STORY-011-no-credentials-in-json.md: full security assessment report
Unit tests: docker run node:20-alpine npx vitest run --config vitest.forceexit.config.ts → all 12 test suites passed (124 tests), all 13 tests in diagramSerializer.test.ts passed

Gitleaks secret scan: docker run zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.18.2 detect --source /work --no-git → 1 finding only, a false positive in git-ignored qa-artifacts/TASK-036/interaction_test.py (string comparison 'password_type == "password"', not a real secret); no secrets in source code
Semgrep SAST: docker run returntocorp/semgrep:latest semgrep scan --config .semgrep/credential-in-export.yaml /work/src/serialization → 0 findings
